“Last Week Tonight” host John Oliver on Sunday took a deep dive into so-called Alligator Alcatraz, the now-shuttered immigration detention facility in the Florida Everglades that was opened by outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R).

With the term-limited DeSantis being floated as a potential successor to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and also rumored to be eyeing another White House run, Oliver argued the closed facility was “still very much worth talking about.”

“For one thing, Alligator Alcatraz is a pretty good encapsulation of the performative cruelty of Trump’s second term,” he said.

“And I am sure that DeSantis, like many of those behind Alligator Alcatraz, would like nothing more than for people to forget about it and move on,” Oliver continued. “But for reasons you’re about to see, that should not happen.”

Oliver laid out “all the costs, human and otherwise, that should be reckoned with going forward.” He detailed reports of inhumane conditions and guards allegedly beating detainees, highlighted how many of those being held were far from “the most vicious people” that Trump had claimed would be sent to the facility, and examined how its estimated cost ballooned to about $1 billion.

Even though it’s “now closed, we should make sure that we remember the utter disgrace that it was,” Oliver concluded. “Everybody involved with Alligator Alcatraz should have the shame of it stick to them for the rest of their lives because it was a shoddy, shameless attempt to gain political points with public cruelty.”
